📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On the back of an iffy Q3, many were hoping Q4 would turn out to be better. Unfortunately, that hasn’t been the case. Especially for those in the XRP and Solana markets.

Recent findings suggest that both these altcoins are in the news today after Roundhill ETF Trust revealed that it will be ditching aims to launch two exchange-traded funds or ETFs tied to them. It cited no specific reason in its filings with the U.S Securities and Exchange Commission for these fresh plans.

The Trust no longer intends to seek effectiveness of the Fund.

It went on to add that “… no securities of the Fund were sold, or will be sold.”.

The registration documents for both these ETFs were filed way back in October 2025. That’s over a year ago. As recently as 06 November, the Trust had submitted an extension. This would have allowed the registrations to become effective by 06 December.

In a recent development, however, an crucial distinction must be made here. It must be pointed out that the ETFs Roundhill was planning to launch were income-focused products. These ETFs would have relied on income generated by trading Options linked to existing crypto prodcuts.

Now, while more recent and fewer in number compared to funds that directly hold these tokens, these products have seen little interest lately.

Consider Amplify’s SOLM, for instance. At the time of writing, it held net assets worth just $1.36 million. This, despite being introduced in November last year. Similarly, the fund manager’s XRPM had net assets worth just over $7.66 million in over a year since its launch.

Recent findings suggest that these numbers are pretty startling, especially when compared to and juxtaposed against the figures reported by other Solana or XRP-focused ETFs. According to SoSoValue, for instance, combined, both these ETF products attracted over $969 million from May to October 2026.

According to recent reports, this, despite recent market weakness hitting these ETF products too. Less than 24 hours ago, XRP ETFs saw outflows of over $6 million, with the Canary XRP ETF (XRPC) and the Grayscale XRP Trust ETF (GXRP) particulalry affected. This, after the week ending ending 13th November saw outflows of $19.1 million. This was the largest single-week withdrawal in nearly eight months.

In a similar vein, the assets under management for Spot Solana ETFs fell from $1.79 billion on 25th September to $947 million on 18th November.

Eight Years: From a Crypto Exchange to a Global Ecosystem Serving 40 Million Users

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (844 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ambcrypto

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • What started eight years ago as a cryptocurrency exchange has evolved into an international business ecosystem of 11 companies serving approximately 40 million consumers worldwide.
  • It has been revealed that the scale of this growth is reflected in WhiteBIT’s $2.8 trillion trading volume in 2026 and more than 5,500 institutional clients.
  • Established in 2025, W Group brought together businesses developed around WhiteBIT under a broader strategy: connecting traditional finance and digital assets while extending their applications into new industries.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

What started eight years ago as a cryptocurrency exchange has evolved into an international business ecosystem of 11 companies serving approximately 40 million consumers worldwide. As WhiteBIT celebrates its eighth anniversary and W Group marks its first year, the milestones highlight a transformation from a single trading platform into a diversified business connecting traditional finance, digital assets, and emerging technologies.

It has been revealed that the scale of this growth is reflected in WhiteBIT’s $2.8 trillion trading volume in 2026 and more than 5,500 institutional clients. Meanwhile, W Group has expanded from eight to 11 companies in one year, growing its combined user base from 35 million to approximately 40 million.

Established in 2025, W Group brought together businesses developed around WhiteBIT under a broader strategy: connecting traditional finance and digital assets while extending their applications into new industries.

The group aims to build more than a portfolio of independent companies. By combining financial infrastructure, technology and expertise, its businesses can develop new services, reach new markets and create opportunities across industries.

It has been revealed that in 2026, W Group expanded well beyond financial services. Dutch sports car manufacturer Spyker joined the group in June, opening opportunities to apply digital finance and blockchain technology to luxury automotive.

According to recent reports, W Group has also made a $400 million investment commitment in SignSplit, the signed-data platform for the AI era. The seed round values SignSplit at $1 billion.

In banking, Georgia-based hashbank, a fully licensed digital bank, combines traditional banking services with cryptocurrency functionality, allowing customers to manage fiat and digital assets within one environment.

Together, these businesses illustrate W Group’s strategy of connecting financial services, technology, and consumer-facing products into an ecosystem where each tech giant can contribute to the growth of the others.

WhiteBIT remains a central pillar of W Group, providing trading infrastructure and digital asset services for retail and institutional clients.

In 2026, the exchange recorded $2.8 trillion in trading volume, with derivatives generating approximately $3.5 billion in daily activity. Its platform now offers nearly 1,200 trading markets.

It has been revealed that trading conditions have also improved. Spot trading volume across WhiteBIT’s flagship BTC, ETH and WBT pairs increased more than fivefold, from $53 billion in 2020 to $276 billion in 2025. Meanwhile, bid-ask spreads across its major markets have narrowed approximately threefold since 2021, reflecting deeper liquidity.

In a recent development, whiteBIT also serves more than 5,500 institutional clients, including funds, brokers and payment providers, through over 20 dedicated products and services. Businesses can access crypto liquidity, manage digital asset transactions and move between fiat currencies and cryptocurrencies through a single platform.

WhiteBIT’s eighth year brought significant regulatory milestones that strengthen the group’s international presence.

In June 2026, WhiteBIT EU secured authorisation under the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) from Austria’s Financial Market Authority, establishing a regulatory foundation for providing crypto-asset services across the European Union.

In May, WhiteBIT launched a dedicated platform for users in the United Kingdom, expanding into another major financial market with demanding regulatory requirements. The company also joined Ghana’s regulatory sandbox in March, contributing to the development of the country’s digital asset regulatory framework.

These developments reflect WhiteBIT’s investment in compliance as a foundation for sustainable international growth.

The growth of the ecosystem is also reflected in WBT, WhiteBIT’s native coin, which reached an all-time high of nearly $88 in September 2026, up from its launch price of $1.62 in 2022.*The milestone reflects WBT’s strong long-term performance alongside the expansion of WhiteBIT and its ecosystem.

WBT’s role is also expanding beyond trading. In November, Whitechain transitioned into an Ethereum Layer 2 network built on the OP Stack in partnership with Optimism, with WBT used to pay transaction fees. Designed to support blockchain applications and financial services, Whitechain has already attracted interest from developers, with more than 140 teams applying to its Builders Program ahead of the network’s public launch planned for later in November.

For W Group, the next stage of growth will focus on connecting its businesses more closely and turning their combined capabilities into latest products and services.

“Eight years ago, we started with one cryptocurrency exchange. Today, we’ve grown into an international group of 11 companies serving around 40 million users. But our ambition has never been simply to build more businesses. We want to connect them in ways that create real value — bringing traditional finance and digital assets closer together, making fresh technologies more accessible and opening opportunities across industries,” mentioned Volodymyr Nosov, Founder and President of W Group.

It has been revealed that looking ahead, W Group aims to strengthen its presence in regulated markets, expand institutional financial services and accelerate blockchain infrastructure development. Its long-term vision is an interconnected ecosystem where banking, payments, digital assets and emerging technologies work together, making financial services more accessible to people and businesses worldwide.

As of Nov. 20, Shiba Inu (SHIB) is about $10 million in market capitalization short of overtaking Bittensor (TAO) for the No. 33 spot in CoinMarketCap's global crypto ranking. TAO has a market cap of $2.18 billion at a price of $186.41, and SHIB has $2.17 billion at $0.000003691 and ranks No. 34.

A gain of about 0.5% in SHIB's price, with TAO's price unchanged, would be enough for the meme coin to take Bittensor's place in the ranking.

Sources indicate that TAO is the token of the Bittensor AI network, and Digital Currency Group (DCG) founder Barry Silbert has been one of its most vocal backers. Silbert also runs Yuma, a DCG organization that builds on Bittensor.

According to recent reports, at Fortune's Brainstorm Tech conference in September 2025, Silbert stated that Bittensor was the thing he had gotten most excited about since Bitcoin. "I want to open up the development and the access to AI, and Bittensor is enabling that," he said at the time. Silbert also said that Bittensor is building a "world wide web of intelligence.".

Sources indicate that on Dec. 30, 2025, DCG's Grayscale filed with the SEC to convert its Grayscale Bittensor Trust into a spot exchange-traded fund on NYSE Arca under the ticker GTAO. The filing came after Bittensor's first halving in mid-December 2025, and at the end of that month, TAO was trading at about $222. "We're pleased to take this early step as we continue to expand the tools available to investors," a Grayscale spokesperson remarked.

Sources indicate that the gap between the two tokens closed because TAO fell. TAO was one of the market's strongest tokens this year. In April, the token was up 55% since January, and in October it rallied again and was up 43% for the year, according to TradingView data.

In a recent development, the November correction erased those gains. On Nov. 20, TAO was trading 16.95% below its January level, and it lost 12.16% over the past week.

SHIB spent most of the year in the red. The meme coin rose about 25% in January, and it has not been in positive territory since February. By Nov. 20, SHIB had lost about 50% since the start of the year, and it fell 13.79% over the past week.

TAO had a 24-hour trading volume of $172.19 million on Nov. 20, and SHIB had $55.17 million, according to CoinMarketCap data. TAO has a maximum supply of 21 million tokens, the same as Bitcoin's, and SHIB has about 589 trillion tokens in circulation.

In a recent development, shiba Inu developer Mazrael responded to the drop on X on Nov. 17. "1 SHIB is always 1 SHIB," he wrote in reply to a user who pointed to the falling price.

AMD fell 8.7%, Micron dropped 10%, and Broadcom lost 6.3%, with 10 of 19 S&P 500 semiconductor stocks down at least 4%.

Nvidia declined 6.9%, extending its losing streak, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell around 4%.

The Nasdaq and S&P 500 weakened as investors reassessed AI valuations, infrastructure spending and the returns from the industry's massive capital commitments.

In a recent development, the AI stock sell-off is widening beyond Nvidia, with semiconductor manufacturers, memory stocks and data-center suppliers facing another round of heavy selling. Micron Technology, Broadcom, AMD and Marvell were among the biggest losers on Friday, while Nvidia extended its decline.

Sources indicate that the momentum of the selloff became more significant: 10 of the 19 S&P 500 semiconductor stocks were down at least 4%, highlighting a sector-wide repricing rather than isolated weakness. Anthropic’s record IPO has failed to restore confidence, leaving investors focused on the cost and profitability of the AI buildout.

Semiconductor stocks were among the market’s weakest performers, with losses extending across chipmakers, equipment manufacturers and AI infrastructure suppliers.

Industry observers note that the breadth of the decline is notable. All 19 S&P 500 semiconductor stocks were trading lower in the latest market reading, while 10 had fallen at least 4%. The group was averaging a decline of approximately 5.7% among the biggest losers.

Industry observers note that nvidia stock fell approximately 7%, putting shares near their lowest levels since June 2025 and extending the firm’s losing streak. The decline has become a broader concern for investors because Nvidia remains a key benchmark for AI spending and semiconductor demand.

AMD, Broadcom and Micron have also faced pressure, despite strong underlying demand for AI chips and memory. Investors are increasingly questioning whether elevated valuations adequately reflect the industry’s capital requirements, competition and potential returns.

The selling has also reached companies further down the AI supply chain. Marvell, Coherent, Bloom Energy, CoreWeave and Nebius have experienced significant declines, suggesting the market is reducing exposure across the broader AI infrastructure trade.

Industry observers note that anthropic’s public debut was expected to provide a fresh catalyst for technology stocks. Instead, the company’s shares fell sharply following their initial surge, while chip stocks continued to weaken.

It has been revealed that ANT stock opened at $111.50, reached $115.10 and closed its first session at $97.17—17% above its $83 IPO price. However, the stock subsequently came under pressure as the broader AI sell-off intensified.

The technology sell-off has weighed heavily on broader indexes. The S&P 500 fell 1.4%, while the Nasdaq declined 2.5% in Friday trading. The Dow Jones remained comparatively resilient, reflecting its lower exposure to technology stocks.

Sources indicate that the market is also approaching a potentially significant losing streak, with the S&P 500 on track for its seventh consecutive daily decline. The weakness follows a sharp previous-session sell-off in which the S&P 500 dropped 2%, the Nasdaq fell 2.3% and the Dow lost 2.2%.

If Nvidia and other major chipmakers stabilize, the sector could recover some of its losses. But continued weakness across semiconductor stocks would signal that investors are still reducing exposure to the AI trade.

For now, the sell-off is less about whether AI demand exists, and more about how much investors are willing to pay for that growth.

Home » Altcoins » Solana (SOL) » GTA VI Launch Sparks $250M Solana Stock Frenzy Over Nvidia.

Tokenized Take-Two shares saw a massive 24-hour trading spike as on-chain markets attract Washington scrutiny.

The long-awaited release of Grand Theft Auto VI didn’t just break gaming records—it briefly turned publisher Take-Two Interactive into the hottest stock on the blockchain, outselling even AI giant Nvidia.

On November 18, decentralized exchange (DEX) trading volume for tokenized Take-Two shares (TTWO) exploded by 578%, jumping from $36.8 million to $249.5 million in a single day, according to Token Terminal data.

That was roughly 2.8 times the $88.1 million traded in tokenized Nvidia (NVDA) shares over the same 24-hour window, accounting for 42% of all on-chain stock trading.

Nearly all of the action, roughly $239 million, or 96% of total volume, happened on Solana via Backpack Securities, a subsidiary of crypto exchange Backpack. Introduced earlier this year, the token is designed to be backed 1:1 by real Take-Two shares held in custody.

Traditional Wall Street traders saw a much calmer reaction: Take-Two’s Nasdaq shares rose 6.2% to close at $216.61 on launch day before pulling back 3.7% to $208.65 the next session.

Despite Take-Two’s one-day viral spike, Nvidia remains the undisputed heavyweight of tokenized equities, boasting a $399.4 million market cap and $2 billion in 30-day trading volume (compared to Take-Two’s $808.1 million).

Overall, tokenized public stocks on Solana have nearly doubled since late October to reach $1.22 billion.

Sources indicate that that rapid growth is drawing fresh scrutiny in Washington. On November 16, four Democratic senators sent a letter to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) questioning how its newly introduced exemption for tokenized securities would address investor protection and anti-money laundering requirements.

Industry observers note that the issue also surfaced during the November 19 Senate Banking Committee confirmation hearing for Kristin Johnson, President Donald Trump’s nominee for the SEC. Johnson indicated that exemptions covering tokenized stocks should eventually be formalized through rules following a public comment period.

According to recent reports, the TTWO spike indicates tokenized stocks can attract event-driven trading on-chain, comparable to some of the largest names in the segment. It also coincides with growing regulatory scrutiny of how tokenized stocks are supervised.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the Cardano [ADA] Treasury Foundation wants 25 million ADA to host 12 events in 2027. Its last $22 million proposal (to buy copper) barely got any votes at all.

Hence, the question — Will this one fare any better?

According to recent reports, on 16th November, the Cardano Foundation filed a proposal to pull 24,995,775 ADA from the network’s treasury. The money would pay for Cardano’s presence at 12 crypto events next year.

Recent findings suggest that some of the biggest names on the circuit are on the list. Consensus in Miami, TOKEN2049 in both Singapore and Upcoming York, Web Summit in Lisbon, and India Blockchain Week in Bangalore.

The run kicks off in February with the Africa Tech Summit in Nairobi.

$2 million will go towards sponsorships and $1.06 million for booths and equipment. Travel is mentioned to cost $702K, while side events will account for $695,000.

Industry observers note that according to the Foundation, none of it covers salaries or profit. Whatever isn’t spent goes back to the treasury.

Recent findings suggest that however, here’s what’s tricky. The Foundation priced ADA at $0.20 to reach its $5 million budget. ADA, however, was valued at $0.15 at press time. At that price, the request is worth about $3.85 million. That is a gap of over $1 million.

For the budget to work as planned, ADA needs to climb by almost 30%. Not impossible, but far from guaranteed.

DReps, the delegates who vote on treasury spending, have until 20th December to decide.

Will 25 million ADA move the price? Probably not. There are about 37.6 billion ADA in circulation. So, this withdrawal will merely be a drop in the ocean.

However, it’s worth pointing out that the chart had bigger problems at press time.

ADA fell from $0.25 in October to $0.155 following a price drop on the 14th.

Is a pause imminent? We might be in the early stages, yes. The RSI fell to 21 after that drop, with the same since climbing to 32, just crossing above its average. The OI has also recovered from about $145 million to $153.5 million. Finally, the funding rates were positive yesterday.

On the contrary, the Chaikin Money Flow was negative, implying that sellers might still have a slight edge.

#41588. Fera Fruit Oil Claims It’s Healthier Than Even Avocado Oil. Should You Make the Switch?

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1088 w)

Fera Fruit Oil Claims It’s Healthier Than Even Avocado Oil. Should You Make the Switch?

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1088 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Menshealth

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that EREWHON, EVERYONE’S FAVORITE love-to-hate overpriced supermarket chain made news recently for switching up their oils.
  • According to recent reports, erewhon isn’t the only firm hawking fera fruit oil as a way to further health-ify their vegan buffalo cauliflower and turmeric chicken tenders.
  • In a recent development, fera fruit oil may sound exotic and healthy (it’s made from fruit?), but as a registered dietitian, I'm not one for assumptions when it comes to food.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that EREWHON, EVERYONE’S FAVORITE love-to-hate overpriced supermarket chain made news recently for switching up their oils. Yes, the certified organic grocer revealed that it's no longer using avocado oil to fry its cafe food. Instead, all 15 locations are switching to certified organic fera fruit oil.

According to recent reports, erewhon isn’t the only firm hawking fera fruit oil as a way to further health-ify their vegan buffalo cauliflower and turmeric chicken tenders. Since launching in April 2026, the oil is now in more than 800 grocers, restaurants, wellness clubs, and luxury hotels like Mezeh Mediterranean Grill and Wynn Las Vegas.

In a recent development, fera fruit oil may sound exotic and healthy (it’s made from fruit?), but as a registered dietitian, I'm not one for assumptions when it comes to food. Especially when it coincides with the peak of seed-oil fear-messaging. Keep reading to learn what this latest-to-the-scene frying oil is and if it's really worth the hype.

Industry observers note that FERA FRUIT OIL is basically palm oil. The firm behind it, Zero Acre Farms, trademarked the name “fera fruit oil” for high oleic palm oil, a type of palm oil that's produced by pressing the fruit of a hybrid palm tree called Oleifera × Guineensis (OxG for short).

According to recent reports, the hybrid plant was originally planted by farmers to reduce bud rot, a disease that notoriously destroys palm crops. A happy side effect was that the oil also ended up having higher oleic acid content, the same heart-healthy monounsaturated fat found in avocado and olive oil.

TRADITIONALLY GROWN PALM has a problematic history of deforestation, but according to Zero Acre Farms, fera fruit oil is a perennial crop that requires just 0.3 acres to produce a ton of oil, using 15 to 20 times less land than soybean or canola oil.

Of course, Zero Acre Farms’ website doesn't cite sources for these numbers, so I did my own digging. Independent research suggests traditional palm yields 3.3 tons per hectare, which is impressive compared to soybean, canola, and sunflower, which collectively produce 0.6 tons per hectare. But OxG palm yields about 1 ton less than traditional palm, which means the demonized seed oils use 3 to 4 times more land, not 15 to 20 times. So the claims seem a bit sensationalized at best?

COMPARED WITH REGULAR palm oil, high oleic palm oil—including the trademarked fera fruit oil—offers a significant nutritional upgrade.

Industry observers note that traditional palm oil contains about 50 percent saturated fat, including about 40 percent oleic acid, and 10 percent polyunsaturated fatty acids. OxG, the hybrid that produces fera fruit, contains 50 percent oleic acid, 33 percent saturated fatty acids, and 12 percent polyunsaturated fatty acids.

As a dietitian, I can get behind these improvements, but the benefits don't translate to real-world benefits quite as well.

According to recent reports, the only way you'll eat fera fruit oil is if you're enjoying pre-made food, most likely fried food, from an establishment using it, as it's not currently available for consumer purchase. And while food fried in fera fruit oil may be slightly nutritionally better than traditional palm oil (which most establishments in the U.S. aren't using anyway), it's still fried food.

This ratio not only contains less saturated fat, but also helps maintain stability over multiple rounds of deep frying compared to other oils. A study presented at the 21st International Oil Palm Conference found that high oleic palm oil lasted more rounds of frying than palm, sunflower, soy, or canola. Because it has less polyunsaturated fat and more monounsaturated and saturated fat, it resists degradation better. This adds up to cost savings, because the oil can be used multiple times, but there's unlikely much of a health advantage. Deep-frying meat and starchy foods in any oil can create harmful compounds, but the link between reusing oil, oil stability, and human health is less clear.

Sources indicate that unrefined high oleic palm oil is rich in antioxidants, including carotenoids and vitamin E. Fera fruit oil is marketed as clean, neutral-tasting, and expeller-pressed, but it offers no guarantee or information on what antioxidants are in the bottle at use or how much.

So while this all sounds great on paper, it's hard to tell how it actually translates into real-world benefits. Is it worth the hype? I'd personally like to see tangible evidence that it does before shelling out extra money for it, and that evidence doesn't seem to exist yet.

Prior to October 15, Erewhon used avocado oil in its fryers. So while there's no arguing that Fera fruit oil has a healthier fatty acid profile than regular palm oil, how does it compare to other fruit oils, like avocado and olive oil, in terms of both health and sustainability?

Industry observers note that while olive oil has strong evidence supporting its positive effects on human health, especially heart health, clinical research on the health effects of high-oleic palm oil, like Fera fruit oil, is limited. In one study, 160 participants had either 25 mL of high oleic palm oil or 25 mL of extra virgin olive oil daily for three months. Both groups had similar reductions in total cholesterol and LDL-cholesterol. While these results are promising, the study was small, and more clinical trials are needed to confidently say high oleic palm oil is as beneficial as olive oil.

Avocado oil has a favorable fatty acid profile of 71 percent monounsaturated fatty acids, 13 percent polyunsaturated fatty acids, and 16 percent saturated fatty acids. Fera fruit oil has more saturated fat and less monounsaturated fat, but no head-to-head studies have tested their health effects.

Recent findings suggest that when an elite grocery store like Erewhon switches to a newly introduced fryer oil, it's easy to assume it's the healthiest choice. But I wouldn't be so quick to jump on board.

It has been revealed that after reviewing the research and understanding the food climate we're currently in, where seed oils are viewed as the culprit of all disease and beef tallow is a cure-all, this honestly seems like just another misguided trend. In the context of reality, when you eat an overall healthy and balanced diet, the occasional fried food, whether it's fried in avocado oil, canola oil, or fera fruit oil, will likely have very little impact on your overall health.

Kelsey Kunik, RDN, is a registered dietician and health writer who covers all-things nutrition for Men's Health and Women's Health.

Industry News: XRP Faces Severe Supply Shortage on Binance

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (280 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: U

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The price of XRP has continued to slump to deeper levels amid the prolonged market volatility.
  • According to the latest data from crypto analytics platform Cryptoquant, XRP is presently facing a severe supply shortage on the world’s largest crypto exchange, Binance.
  • According to the data, XRP’s Supply Shortage Index on Binance has surged to 2.4 as of November 19 despite the asset’s extreme price weakness in recent days.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The price of XRP has continued to slump to deeper levels amid the prolonged market volatility. However, recent onchain data has shown an unexpected trend in exchange activity.

According to the latest data from crypto analytics platform Cryptoquant, XRP is presently facing a severe supply shortage on the world’s largest crypto exchange, Binance.

According to the data, XRP’s Supply Shortage Index on Binance has surged to 2.4 as of November 19 despite the asset’s extreme price weakness in recent days.

Notably, the data further demonstrates that the metric has surpassed the previous reading of 2.09 recorded on July 6, marking a five-month high in XRP’s supply shortage index.

It is vital to note that readings above +2 are a strong indication of severely tightened supply, which means that the amount of XRP available on the exchange has decreased significantly.

While negative readings often mean the opposite, this means that XRP has witnessed a sharp reversal from the supply level seen on September 27.

Recent findings suggest that at the time, the index stood at -1.5 while XRP traded above $1.50, signaling an abundance of XRP on Binance. This means that more tokens were available for trading during the period, which potentially added to selling pressure.

While that is no longer the case, the latest data demonstrates that the XRP supply index has jumped by 3.9 points in just 53 days, moving from supply abundance to severe supply tightness in just about two months.

This typically suggests that XRP is being aggressively moved out of exchanges despite its prolonged price weakness, potentially driving a rebound in the demand for XRP, which could eventually trigger a price recovery.

Google shipped Gemini 4 Neon on Wednesday, its fourth frontier model release in three weeks, and on the eve of the heavily anticipated Anthropic IPO.

This isn’t just a normal model release. For one, it’s incredibly good. Neon posts 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index against 59 for Claude Opus 5.5 and 57 for GPT-6.2 Sol. But there will be massive volatility, and it’s very likely to trade under that $83 level over the coming days and weeks. Especially given the latest (surprise) headwinds from Google with its outperforming model.

According to recent reports, we will find out soon enough. Good luck to everyone trading it today.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Anthropic’s post-IPO performance appears to have created a volatile market setup.
  • On the technical side, ANT opened at $111.50, around 34% above its $83 IPO price, before losing much of its early gains and closing at $97.17.
  • Naturally, this raises a question: Is crypto’s weakness simply a result of ANT-driven volatility?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anthropic’s post-IPO performance appears to have created a volatile market setup.

On the technical side, ANT opened at $111.50, around 34% above its $83 IPO price, before losing much of its early gains and closing at $97.17. This reveals that initial demand was strong, but profit-taking rapidly kicked in. The impact also seems to have spilled over into crypto, with the total market cap forming its third consecutive lower low at $2.08 trillion, a level last seen in early Q3.

Naturally, this raises a question: Is crypto’s weakness simply a result of ANT-driven volatility? Interestingly, recent Glassnode data points to a possible link. As the chart below indicates, Anthropic futures on crypto platforms recorded $9.5 billion in trading volume ahead of its Nasdaq debut. In comparison, SpaceX, the largest IPO on record, attracted $3.9 billion in pre-listing futures volume before its June debut.

In essence, ANT’s pre-IPO futures generated more than 2.4x SpaceX’s.

It has been revealed that this highlights how much larger speculative interest in ANT was compared to SpaceX, setting a fresh record for pre-IPO trading activity on crypto platforms. However, the initial hype quickly turned into profit-taking, with ANT dropping 13% from its opening price. This shift in sentiment may have added to Bitcoin’s [BTC] selling pressure, especially as liquidation activity picked up alongside the broader market breakdown.

So, is Bitcoin’s latest breakdown the start of an overall deleveraging process in crypto markets? In other words, could IPO-driven volatility have accelerated long liquidations, forced overleveraged traders out of positions, and triggered a general market reset?

It looks like ANT’s futures activity on crypto platforms may have added to the selling pressure.

According to CoinGlass, over $700 million worth of positions have been liquidated in the last 24 hours. Of that amount, nearly $600 million was long positions, indicating that leveraged bulls have been badly hit by the correction. However, can this flush-out in Futures markets lead to a rebalance?

Recent findings suggest that worth mentioning here is the ongoing liquidity drain. In the last 30 days, $11.5 billion has left the stablecoin supply. That outflow is greater than it was in the aftermath of the Terra collapse in 2022. While many in the crypto market are looking at Bitcoin’s price movements, the real problem is the decreasing capital in crypto.

Why does this matter? Lower stablecoin supply means less available liquidity to support buying activity, which could keep pressure on Bitcoin and the broader market.

Sources indicate that so, while ANT-related volatility may have contributed to market deleveraging, liquidity is still very poor for a sustained recovery. In this context, ANT’s IPO may have added to an already fragile market, while concerns around its valuation may also “continue” to create a risk-off sentiment in U.S. markets.

Against this backdrop, a drop in the total crypto market cap below $2 trillion cannot be ruled out.

ANT’s IPO may have added to Bitcoin’s fear and increased crypto selling.

Weak liquidity could keep pressure on crypto, putting the $2 trillion market cap at risk.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The flagship coin has crashed to a fresh 4.5-month low amid persistent institutional outflows totaling billions from cryptocurrency exchange-traded funds (ETFs).
  • $BTC hasn't formed a higher high for 16 consecutive days now.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitcoin (BTC), the world’s largest cryptocurrency, is flashing a major, ‘scary’ technical signal that was absent even during its last major crashes in February and June 2026.

The flagship coin has crashed to a fresh 4.5-month low amid persistent institutional outflows totaling billions from cryptocurrency exchange-traded funds (ETFs).

$BTC hasn't formed a higher high for 16 consecutive days now. This didn't even happen during the Feb 2026 and June 2026 crashes. https://t.co/I6IPmdueEc.

Sources indicate that bitcoin has failed to form a higher high for the past 16 days. This is a very long stretch, one that was absent during Bitcoin’s February and June crashes.

In a recent development, A higher high, in the context of technical analysis, is formed when an asset’s price reaches a newly introduced high point above its previous swing high. The absence of higher highs signals that buyers are having a hard time taking back control of the market.

The latest Bitcoin price action adds further to concerns surrounding the future of the flagship cryptocurrency.

Earlier today, BTC crashed to $61,225, its lowest price point in around four and a half months.

Bitcoin's failure to create higher highs despite several attempts to recover reveals that selling pressure remains quite high.

Nevertheless, this technical pattern of 16 days without a higher high does not necessarily spell more pain for Bitcoin. If the cryptocurrency can decisively push above recent resistance zones, it may be a sign that buyers are starting to make a comeback.

Bitcoin is facing persistent withdrawals of huge amounts of money from U.S.-based spot Bitcoin ETFs.

In a recent development, blackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) witnessed its biggest-ever daily net outflow on Nov. 19.

The crypto fund suffered a whopping $541.1 million in net withdrawals on the day. At the same time, total net outflows from U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs amounted to around $582.3 million across the entire market.

More alarmingly, the fresh wave of withdrawals brings cumulative net outflows from U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs to around $3.47 billion so far this November.

The ETFs have seen negative net flows on 12 of the first 14 trading days of the month.

  • As the global cryptocurrency market cap fell 2.2% to $2.21 trillion in the last 24 hours at press time, the Crypto Fear & Greed Index slid to 12, indicating “extreme fear.”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The early hours of the 20th of November saw Bitcoin [BTC] trading at $61,678 after a staggering 9.7% drop in the last 24 hours. Ethereum [ETH], following the crypto bloodbath, traded at $1,732 after experiencing a 3.7% slide in this time frame.

The crypto market’s current downfall is primarily due to persistent Spot ETF outflows and lingering fallout from last month’s Binance breach, which are making investors wary.

As the global cryptocurrency market cap fell 2.2% to $2.21 trillion in the last 24 hours at press time, the Crypto Fear & Greed Index slid to 12, indicating “extreme fear.”.

After $306.5 million left Spot Bitcoin ETFs on the 18th of November, CoinGlass data showed that $582.3 million in outflows on the following day,  pushing this month’s outflows well past the $2.9 billion mark. Continued ETF bleeding signals that buyers continue to exit, leaving the market quite vulnerable to macro volatility.

Similarly, minutes from the October FOMC meeting, released on the 18th of November, showed that nearly all officials expect further rate hikes. Notably, Governor Christopher Waller even floated a half-point move for December.

With the Fed target at 3.75%–4.00%, digital assets will not have an easy battle.

Ever since investors have moved away from crypto and into AI, the former’s fall has been nearly constant. For the uninitiated, on the 18th of November, Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share, thus valuing the AI tech giant at roughly $1.5 trillion.

The news drew massive investor attention, pulling capital away from crypto markets as a result.

Regardless, the long-term sentiment of crypto investors has already been sullied due to the October 29 Binance hack that resulted in $6.3 billion in stolen funds.

The crypto bloodbath will likely continue unless ETF flows stabilize or the Fed signals a pause. With the December 9 FOMC meeting as the only upcoming checkpoint, 60,000 is the next level for traders to watch. Losing it can tip Bitcoin deeper into the mid-50,000s.

Presently, only 130 crypto whale wallets qualified for Trump’s fancy memecoin dinner at the golf club.

Just 130 crypto wallets secured seats for the November 22 TRUMP token holder dinner at Donald Trump’s Virginia golf club, leaving dozens of the 185 available places unclaimed. The Official Trump token was trading near record lows at the time of the close.

Recent findings suggest that the event is designed to reward the largest holders, with the top 29 wallets also eligible for a VIP reception. Contest participants held roughly $8.6 million in tokens combined when the qualification period ended, a sharp drop in engagement from the project’s first holder dinner.

BREAKING: 🇺🇸 Trump will host an exclusive dinner for the top 185 $TRUMP holders this Sunday.The coin is down 99% from its peak. pic.twitter.com/NxizWHlrVg.

Ranking was based on time-weighted holdings, which encouraged accumulation and retention through the window.

Industry observers note that more than 5,000 eligible holders reportedly did not register. The leaderboard’s combined value represented only a small fraction of TRUMP’s roughly $268 million market capitalization.

Industry observers note that TRUMP was trading around $0.95 in the latest reporting, down roughly 46% over the prior month after setting a record low near $0.896 on November 14. The token remains well below its peak, with one account describing it as down almost 99% from its high.

Recent findings suggest that large holders added to positions during the dip. Nansen data indicated the top 100 wallets increased their combined holdings by 1.27% over 30 days, while a separate whale cohort expanded holdings by 26.63%. Exchange balances fell slightly over the same period.

Holding incentives are temporary.

It has been revealed that top-ranked winners risk losing VIP benefits if balances drop below specified levels before the event, and lower-ranked winners can forfeit their seat by selling more than half their qualifying balance. Those restrictions expire once the dinner is over.

Ahead of the 2025 dinner, 92 of 220 invited holders reportedly sold their entire positions before the event.

A Super Bowl-themed leaderboard planned for February 2027 may give some buyers a reason to stay involved, but it does not remove the immediate question of whether winners will take liquidity afterward.

Shiba Inu’s layer-2 network, Shibarium, is experiencing a major slowdown as daily network activity has fallen to three-digit figures (fewer than 1,000 transactions), hitting lows not seen in months.

It has been revealed that shibarium processed 546 transactions, according to Shibariumscan data, marking a slower period for the layer-2 network after activity spiked to a high of 6,370 on October 31, 2026. Transaction activity declined afterward, and the decline intensified amid the sell-off that hit the market in recent weeks.

The latest figures suggest that fewer transactions are taking place across Shibarium compared with periods of stronger activity. The key question now is whether Shibarium can regain momentum in the coming weeks.

Meanwhile, development continues behind the scenes for the Shiba Inu layer-2 network, as long-time Shiba Inu community member and developer Mazrael revealed a big batch of contracts deployed on Puppynet, Shibarium's testnet.

But in the meantime, Shibarium’s fall to three-digit activity levels is a major slowdown that SHIB holders and ecosystem watchers will be watching closely.

Shiba Inu's on-chain holders increased as the number of wallets holding SHIB hit 1,700,930 on November 19, 2026.

According to the latest figures shared by Etherscan SHIB, an X account dedicated to providing updates on the SHIB ecosystem, the cryptocurrency added 236 new on-chain holders in a single day, taking its total past the 1.7 million milestone.

Sources indicate that the month of November has also seen consistent growth, with SHIB adding 4,520 holders since the start of the month. The broader 2026 trend is even more pronounced, with the number of holders of the token increasing by 152,300 since the beginning of the year.

While Shiba Inu's latest milestone seems remarkable, Mazrael suggested that the Shib ecosystem, including Shibarium, might have more holders than indicated, with 1.4 million holders of Binance-pegged SHIB on the BNB Chain.

"Shibarium has more holders than those you listed, though. But yeah. Well, there are also 1.4 million holders of Binance-pegged SHIB on BNB. But that's not actually CCIP SHIB; it is a peg," Mazrael wrote.

#41571. Quantum Upgrade Could Be 'Particularly Challenging' for Blockchains: IOSCO

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (804 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Decrypt ↗ Open Full Page

Quantum Upgrade Could Be 'Particularly Challenging' for Blockchains: IOSCO

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (804 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Decrypt

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Financial markets, including crypto, need to start preparing now for quantum computers capable of breaking the cryptography that secures them, according to the world's main forum for securities regulators.
  • It has been revealed that A "sufficiently capable" quantum computer could undermine widely used public-key cryptography that supports critical functions across financial markets, the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) remarked in a report published on Thursday.
  • "Practical quantum computers capable of compromising widely used cryptography do not yet exist, but the scale and duration of the transition mean the financial sector should start preparing today," IOSCO Board Chair Jean-Paul Servais noted in a statement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Financial markets, including crypto, need to start preparing now for quantum computers capable of breaking the cryptography that secures them, according to the world's main forum for securities regulators.

It has been revealed that A "sufficiently capable" quantum computer could undermine widely used public-key cryptography that supports critical functions across financial markets, the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) remarked in a report published on Thursday. The cyber readiness challenge posed by quantum computing "is immediate and requires action," it said.

"Practical quantum computers capable of compromising widely used cryptography do not yet exist, but the scale and duration of the transition mean the financial sector should start preparing today," IOSCO Board Chair Jean-Paul Servais noted in a statement.

The 63-page report cited conservative estimates that such machines could emerge between 2030 and 2035. Several industry participants consulted by IOSCO went further, arguing that firms should prepare for the possibility that they arrive within five years, potentially accelerated by AI.

Industry observers note that IOSCO stated the migration may be particularly challenging for blockchains, because cryptography is embedded in their core architecture and any change requires coordinated action across decentralized networks. Public blockchains such as Ethereum, Solana and Tron rely heavily on elliptic curve cryptography to verify identities and validate transactions, and a powerful enough quantum computer could derive private keys from exposed public keys, a scenario known as "Q-Day.".

Swapping in quantum-resistant signatures comes at a cost. Signatures under ML-DSA-44, a post-quantum standard from the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, are about 2,420 bytes, roughly 35 to 40 times larger than today's 64-byte elliptic curve signatures, the report remarked. It cited evidence from a quantum-resistant Solana testnet that saw throughput fall by about 90% when post-quantum signatures replaced existing ones.

Sources indicate that because the cryptography sits in transaction formats and consensus rules, replacing it requires hard forks, and decentralized networks have no way to force quick adoption, making migration "slow and fragmented," IOSCO remarked. Accounts and smart contracts still controlled by vulnerable keys could stay exposed after a network adds quantum-resistant options, and the path to quantum resistance for Bitcoin wallets remains uphill.

Industry observers note that wallet makers face their own trade-offs. SHRINCS, the leading candidate for a post-quantum Bitcoin signature scheme, offers "stateful" signatures that are about 10 times smaller but can expose funds to theft if keys are reused beyond a set signing budget, Trezor CTO Tomáš Sušánka has noted. Trezor is considering making the larger, safer stateless option the default, and hardware wallets will also need post-quantum cryptography for firmware and device authentication, he added.

Sources indicate that the report distinguished "on-spend" attacks, in which an attacker races to exploit a public key revealed by a pending transaction, from "at-rest" attacks on keys left exposed for longer. Dormant or abandoned coins pose a particular problem where their holders can't move them. Crypto firms have formed a quantum alliance as some 6 million BTC sit in exposed addresses, and Bitcoin developer Cory Fields has proposed "quantum landmines" to make attacks on such coins costly.

Layer-2 networks are not insulated either. Optimistic rollups could face forged signatures during their dispute windows, typically seven days on Ethereum, and many zero-knowledge rollups use SNARK proofs that rely on elliptic curves. Hash-based STARK proofs are more resistant, but a rollup is only as safe as the layer-1 contracts, bridges and governance keys it depends on, the report remarked.

Developers are already working on fixes. Researchers have proposed several ways to make Bitcoin quantum-safe, StarkWare has shown a quantum-safe Bitcoin transaction, and Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has said the network is betting its future on quantum resistance.

IOSCO said firms should migrate to post-quantum cryptography and build "crypto-agility," the ability to revision cryptographic systems without major redesign. Quantum key distribution could complement those measures on selected high-security channels, it added.

Most preparations across financial markets are still at an early stage, focused on awareness, governance, training and identifying vulnerable systems, according to the report, which drew on a March 2026 survey of members of IOSCO's Fintech Task Force and discussions with experts. Some respondents described "quantum-procrastination," in which firms put off action while waiting for clearer regulatory signals or wider adoption.

No surveyed jurisdiction reported operational deployment of quantum computing in regulated financial services. The watchdog also urged regulators to act against "quantum washing," in which firms overstate the role, maturity or performance of quantum technology. IOSCO said it will treat quantum as a priority in 2027, focusing on raising awareness across the financial ecosystem.

Quantum hardware is advancing rapidly. IBM has claimed a trusted quantum advantage, and Google has said it has cracked some of the field's biggest bottlenecks.

  • The growing role of financial advisors and wealth management platforms played a major role.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that things have changed dramatically since the third quarter of 2026, when institutional interest in Bitcoin [BTC] increased. After three quarters of net selling, institutional investors resumed net purchases of spot Bitcoin exchange-traded products (ETPs).

Recent findings suggest that according to Alex Thorn from Galaxy Research, institutions added approximately 49,229 BTC-equivalent during the three-month period. Notably, by the 30th of September, institutional investment managers held a record 356,491 BTC-equivalent, worth approximately $29.78 billion.

The growing role of financial advisors and wealth management platforms played a major role.

Together, they held 144,307 BTC-equivalent by the end of September, representing 40.5% of all Bitcoin ETP holdings reported by institutional managers. If looked back, their holdings have increased for nine consecutive quarters and are now 3.3 times higher than their March 2024 levels.

That being said, large banks played a major role in this accumulation, with Wells Fargo, Bank of America, and Morgan Stanley being among the biggest buyers during Q3.

In a recent development, wells Fargo alone added 14,636 BTC-equivalent, taking its total holdings to 30,553 BTC-equivalent, making it the largest institutional holder of U.S. spot Bitcoin ETPs, overtaking Jane Street.

Institutional ownership also shifted, with hedge funds dropping from 50.6% in December 2024 to 19%, while financial advisors and wealth platforms increased their exposure. Of this, BlackRock’s IBIT accounted for 65.2% of institutional Bitcoin ETP holdings.

That remarked, Bitcoin ETP holdings fell by 38,531 BTC between the 30th of September and the 16th of November.

However, the tokenized ETP sector continued to struggle, with its market capitalization falling 6.2% to $595 million and trading volume declining to $160 million, as previously reported by AMBCrypto.

Recent findings suggest that this comes as Bitcoin spot ETFs recorded net inflows of $2.65 billion in September 2026 and $3.52 billion in August, while July saw smaller inflows of $172.43 million. However, the trend reversed in October, with $515.03 million in net outflows, followed by significantly larger outflows of $3.47 billion in November 2026.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. NEAR Protocol (NEAR) fell 11.41% on Nov. 20 and traded at $2.84, according to TradingView data. In early October, the token was trading near $6, and it has lost about half of its value since then.

Recent findings suggest that over the same period, the volume of NEAR Intents went up. "NEAR went from $6 to $3 in about a month. funny thing is, NEAR Intents is doing more volume now than it did in october," NEAR ecosystem contributor Evgeny Haenko wrote on X on Nov. 20.

According to Haenko, NEAR Intents averaged around $129 million in daily volume in October, and in November it was processing around $134 million a day. "The price got cut in half, the business didn't slow down at all. hard for me to be bearish here," he wrote.

NEAR Intents lets users swap assets across more than 30 blockchains, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and XRP. The service is built into wallets such as Ledger, Trust Wallet and Brave. Over the past year, its trading volume grew 7.1 times to $39.5 billion.

NEAR Intents has collected about $63 million in fees in total, and the network keeps about 29% of that amount. Fees on the NEAR Intents interface, payments from B2B partners and the spread on better-than-market trades accounted for 16.3%, 9.9% and 2.8% of the fees, respectively. Over the last 30 days, the protocol earned about $1.8 million, compared with $2.2 million in October.

Since February 2026, the protocol has used NEAR Intents revenue to buy NEAR on the market. More than 1.84 million NEAR have gone to the buyback wallet so far, and that is 41.6% of all distributed onchain revenue. Base transaction fees on the network are burned in full.

Recent findings suggest that in early November, the NEAR community also voted to cut the maximum annual issuance from 2.5% to 1.6% over two years. The proposal, HSP-029, went through House of Stake, NEAR's governance initiative, and Haenko is one of its participants.

It has been revealed that on Sept. 29, Bitwise introduced the first U.S. spot NEAR ETF on NYSE Arca under the ticker NRR. Two days later, on Oct. 1, NEAR Intents paused its services after an exploit that cost about $3.8 million, and the team promised to compensate consumers in full. The exploiter later returned the funds. "The funds from the $3.8M NEAR Intents hack were sent back in full," NEAR Intents general manager Alex Shevchenko said at the time.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The bitcoin price slipped to near $61,500 on Friday morning, according to Look Into Bitcoin data, as a selloff in technology stocks that followed Anthropic’s Nasdaq debut spread to Asian markets and dragged bitcoin to its lowest level since July.
  • Bitcoin first broke below $62,000 on Thursday evening, after Thursday afternoon’s report revealed it giving back a rebound toward $64,000.
  • Sources indicate that the selling started in Asia.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The bitcoin price slipped to near $61,500 on Friday morning, according to Look Into Bitcoin data, as a selloff in technology stocks that followed Anthropic’s Nasdaq debut spread to Asian markets and dragged bitcoin to its lowest level since July.

Bitcoin first broke below $62,000 on Thursday evening, after Thursday afternoon’s report revealed it giving back a rebound toward $64,000. The bitcoin price then slid to nearly $61,200 during Asian trading before bouncing back above $61,700. Friday marks a third straight day of losses.

Sources indicate that the selling started in Asia. South Korea’s Kospi slid more than 5%, with chipmakers SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics down around 6%. The Korea Exchange halted program selling for five minutes after the drop, while Japan’s Nikkei fell as much as 4.85% to a seven-month low.

U.S. futures pointed lower too. Nasdaq-100 futures fell more than 1.7% and S&P 500 futures dropped 0.8%, Yahoo Finance reported. Gold futures lost 3%. The S&P 500 is pointing to a seventh straight daily decline, its longest losing streak since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020.

In a recent development, anthropic shares fell 8% in premarket trading after closing their first session at $97.17, up 17% from the $83 IPO price. Nvidia was down about 2.4% and AMD fell nearly 7%, CNBC reported. Hawkish signals from Federal Reserve officials this week also weighed on sentiment, Reuters said.

Recent findings suggest that bitcoin funds are feeling the pressure. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) recorded $541.1 million in net outflows on Thursday, its largest single-day outflow since launch. That topped the previous record of $528.3 million set on Jan. 30. The fund bled $2 billion over nine straight days of outflows earlier this month.

Leveraged traders took heavy losses as the bitcoin price broke support. Bitcoin liquidations hit $712.9 million over 24 hours, with $614 million coming from long positions. Open interest in bitcoin futures fell to $18 billion from $20 billion a week ago, and funding rates flipped broadly negative as traders unwound their bets.

According to recent reports, traders are now watching whether the bitcoin price can hold the $60,000 area. A large pocket of long positions sits in the $60,500 to $60,900 band, just below the current price, and could come into play on a further drop. Bitcoin is also on track for a seventh straight weekly loss, which would be its second-longest losing streak after nine weeks of declines in 2022.

Crypto stocks pointed lower in premarket trading. Strategy (MSTR) traded near $83.90, down about 2.6% from Thursday’s close of $86.13, after the stock fell for a sixth straight day on Thursday. Coinbase (COIN) slipped about 2.7% to near $106.

Bitcoin miners fell harder. IREN (IREN) dropped about 4.4%, CleanSpark (CLSK) lost about 3.6% and MARA Holdings (MARA) declined about 3.4%. Riot Platforms (RIOT) was down about 3.3%. IREN has also been under pressure as investors reassess AI infrastructure stocks. Delays in bringing some of its capacity online led Microsoft to spend less with the miner than planned last quarter.

Longer-term buyers have not left entirely. Institutional investors added 49,229 BTC through U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs in the third quarter, lifting their holdings to a record 356,491 BTC. Swiss bank Sygnum called the current downturn the shallowest bear market for bitcoin to date, putting the drawdown at around 54% compared with declines of more than 70% in previous cycles.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $61,800.

Famous financial educator and author of "Rich Dad Poor Dad" Robert Kiyosaki has disclosed when investors should begin accumulating Bitcoin (BTC) during the current cryptocurrency market bloodbath.

While he is consistently bullish on Bitcoin, Kiyosaki is asking investors to be patient and not buy the flagship cryptocurrency before the current crash ends.

Industry observers note that in his latest X post on Nov. 20, Kiyosaki shared an vital investment lesson and warned his followers against catching a falling knife.

"Never grab a falling knife," Kiyosaki warned.

The financial guru suggested that this means investors should wait until the cryptocurrency market crash ends before buying more Bitcoin.

"That means wait for the crash to end….before buying," Kiyosaki elaborated.

Notably, Kiyosaki shared that he began buying Bitcoin when its price was around $20,000 after another major market crash.

The best-selling author hinted that he is planning to do the same during the current market downturn.

"Will wait for Bitcoin bottom again," Kiyosaki noted.

The financial educator reminded his followers of one of his important investment tips.

"Your profit is made when you buy….not when you sell," Kiyosaki noted.

Basically, the financial educator suggested that investors should prioritize finding good entry prices rather than trying to buy Bitcoin while its price keeps dropping.

However, Kiyosaki did not specify a Bitcoin price target or how he is going to know that the market has bottomed out.

Kiyosaki's remarks follow another devastating Bitcoin crash that took the flagship cryptocurrency to its lowest level in more than four months.

Recent findings suggest that on Nov. 20, the world's largest cryptocurrency crashed below the key psychological price level of $60,000 for the first time since July.

According to Reuters, Bitcoin crashed to around $59,381. Bitcoin shed over 3% in a single trading session.

Interestingly, BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) saw a record $541.1 million in daily outflows.

In a recent development, overall, the latest data highlights that November has seen total net outflows from U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs worth around $3.47 billion.

Interestingly, Kiyosaki has shared his excitement about buying Bitcoin during major market corrections several times.

Earlier, on Nov. 20, Kiyosaki described the ongoing market crash as a possible buying opportunity. He suggested that experienced investors are sitting back and waiting to accumulate while bad investors are trying to sell everything.

It has been revealed that "I am most excited about Bitcoin's crash. Waiting to buy more," Kiyosaki declared.

Kiyosaki stressed that Bitcoin has a limited supply of 21 million coins. He believes that this scarcity makes Bitcoin vastly different from traditional government-issued currencies.

VanEck ends Gemini deal for 3 crypto ETFs – What’s next for VSOL?

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that vanEck has terminated Gemini as custodian and clearing agent for three U.S.
  • As per three 8-K filings from the 19th of November, VanEck Digital Assets delivered written termination notices to Gemini Trust Firm on the 16th of November, with the contract set to officially end on 16th February.
  • The notice ended custody and clearing arrangements for the VanEck Bitcoin ETF (HODL) and the VanEck Ethereum ETF (ETHV).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that vanEck has terminated Gemini as custodian and clearing agent for three U.S. crypto ETFs. In doing so, it has made Coinbase Custody its sole remaining safekeeper, thus putting into jeopardy the Solana fund’s staking future.

As per three 8-K filings from the 19th of November, VanEck Digital Assets delivered written termination notices to Gemini Trust Firm on the 16th of November, with the contract set to officially end on 16th February.

The notice ended custody and clearing arrangements for the VanEck Bitcoin ETF (HODL) and the VanEck Ethereum ETF (ETHV).

The third ETF, the VanEck Solana ETF (VSOL), is the most affected one in this regard, because there is no news on who will take over staking services for it. Market participants are assuming it is Coinbase, but as of now, there is no confirmation yet.

Industry observers note that as expected, the filings have opened a series of questions, as they have not established the allocation of assets between Gemini and Coinbase. This, in turn, has made it impossible to quantify precisely what Gemini is losing in dollar terms.

The filing also failed to explain why VanEck chose to terminate the agreements now, with roughly three months of notice before the effective date. Moreover, they did not even address the staking question that matters most for VSOL shareholders.

Sources indicate that this comes as the crypto ETF landscape has been in a consolidation for a while now, with Coinbase already being a custodian for most U.S. Spot crypto ETFs.

All in all, VanEck’s current decision to put an end to its Gemini arrangements has left it with a single custodian across all three funds and a massive unresolved operational gap.

What’s left now is that by 16th February, 2027, the firm will have to find a new staking provider for VSOL.

Bitcoin Hovers Just Above Average Holder’s Cost Basis as Price Keeps Dipping

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (621 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bitcoinmagazine

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bitcoin is trading just above its realized price, the average cost of every coin on the network, and a break below that level would put the average holder at a loss for the first time since early 2023, Glassnode, an onchain analytics firm posted Friday.
  • According to recent reports, the price of bitcoin sat near $61,700 on Friday after sliding below $62,000.
  • It has been revealed that the margin is thin.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitcoin is trading just above its realized price, the average cost of every coin on the network, and a break below that level would put the average holder at a loss for the first time since early 2023, Glassnode, an onchain analytics firm posted Friday.

According to recent reports, the price of bitcoin sat near $61,700 on Friday after sliding below $62,000. The realized price is a measure of what holders paid, not where the market trades. When bitcoin trades above it, the typical coin is sitting on a gain. Below it, the typical coin is underwater.

It has been revealed that the margin is thin. The firm noted the MVRV ratio, which compares bitcoin’s market value with its realized value, sits “just above 1.” A reading of 1 means the market price has fallen all the way to the realized price.

Realized price values each coin at the price it last moved on the blockchain, then averages across the supply. Look Into Bitcoin describes it as bitcoin’s average cost basis. Because it tracks the price when coins last changed hands, it moves far more slowly than the market.

In a recent development, the MVRV ratio expresses the same idea as a multiple. Above 1, holders are in profit on average. Below 1, they are not. A reading just above 1 means the market price is only a sliver higher than what the average coin cost.

Industry observers note that the firm did not give the exact realized price in its post, which included a chart. That leaves the exact cushion between today’s price and the average cost basis unstated. Bitcoin Magazine Pro’s full realized price chart sits behind a login, so the current level could not be confirmed independently for this report.

Sources indicate that “The average Bitcoin holder is still in profit,” the firm wrote. “The margin is thin.”.

The slide has come with heavy selling from funds. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) lost about $541 million on Thursday, its largest one-day outflow since it launched in January 2024, Bloomberg reported. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $582 million in total that day.

The selling stands out against the buying earlier in the fall. Institutions piled into bitcoin ETFs through the third quarter, pushing their combined holdings to a record, Bitcoin Magazine reported this week.

Industry observers note that leveraged traders took losses too. More than $700 million in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, and about 86% of them were bets on higher prices. Bitcoin accounted for roughly $200 million of the total.

CoinShares head of research James Butterfill said the drop is part of a longer downturn rather than the start of a newly introduced one. “I see this as a continuation of the existing bear market rather than the start of another,” he said in a note dated Nov. 18.

It has been revealed that the note frames Friday’s price action as a late stage of a decline that began well before November. Butterfill pointed to whale selling that weighed on prices from late 2025, expectations of higher interest rates and weakness in technology stocks, all of which have kept buyers cautious.

Industry observers note that “Our base case remains range trading around USD 60k to 90k through much of 2027, until falling inflation gives monetary policy room to ease,” he said. “Geopolitics will have a considerable say in that.”.

A move through the realized price would put bitcoin near the bottom edge of that range. The firm stated holders as a group have not been in loss since early 2023.

A sustained breakout, Butterfill said, would likely require “a change in the policy outlook, renewed whale participation or both.”.

Navigating the Unpredictable Ride of COPD

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1318 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Menshealth

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, HOOVES THUNDER AGAINST packed dirt as the bull bucks to the left and the rider leans right, tightening his grip on the rope.
  • Industry observers note that the unexpected twists and turns of a bull ride may feel familiar to people living with inadequately controlled chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).
  • Recent findings suggest that mark H., 60, has experienced the challenges that can come with COPD since he was diagnosed in 2010.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sponsored by Sanofi and Regeneron.

In a recent development, HOOVES THUNDER AGAINST packed dirt as the bull bucks to the left and the rider leans right, tightening his grip on the rope. Just as he finds his balance, another sudden buck or turn can change the course of the ride.

Industry observers note that the unexpected twists and turns of a bull ride may feel familiar to people living with inadequately controlled chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Not knowing when breathing challenges or a flare-up—a period when breathing becomes more difficult than usual that can last for several days—might occur can make everyday life feel unpredictable.

Recent findings suggest that mark H., 60, has experienced the challenges that can come with COPD since he was diagnosed in 2010. “COPD isn’t easy to navigate, and it can be a frightening condition to face,” he says. “I tried to ignore my diagnosis early on because I didn’t want to believe it, and I didn’t want to think about how it might affect my life. But ignoring it didn’t stop my COPD from making itself known. Shortness of breath was really impacting my day to day.”.

Industry observers note that with support and clinical intervention, Mark was able to better manage his COPD and get back to doing more of the things he loves. Now, he wants others living with COPD to know help is available to manage their condition.

COPD IS A complex and progressive disease that can make breathing more difficult over time.

Recent findings suggest that COPD can be caused by inflammation in the airways that causes damage to parts of your lungs. Patients with COPD may also have chronic bronchitis and/or emphysema.

In a recent development, people with COPD can experience persistent cough, excessive mucus production, wheezing, chest tightness, and shortness of breath. Understanding COPD is key, and recognizing when the disease may not be adequately controlled is critical. Living with uncertainty around flare-ups can carry an emotional weight as well, states Corinne Young, nurse practitioner, pulmonary disease specialist, who is the Founder/Executive Director of the Association of Pulmonary Advanced Practice Providers.

Flare-ups, also known as exacerbations, are the worsening of COPD symptoms over several days. They can happen to anyone with COPD. During a flare-up, difficulty breathing, wheezing, and coughing can intensify and take longer to resolve. Even one flare-up can lead to permanent lung damage.

Young, who in addition to seeing patients, competes in team roping at rodeos, knows the importance of paying attention to changing conditions—a perspective she brings to helping patients recognize when their COPD may be inadequately controlled.

Sources indicate that “The biggest predictor of a flare-up is a previous flare-up, and they start to get closer and closer together,” Young explains. For example, someone may experience a flare-up or exacerbation once every two years, then once a year, then every six months, then every three. “Inflammatory responses in the body drive these exacerbations, and that may lower lung function,” Young adds. That decline can increase the risk of additional flare-ups, perpetuating the cycle.

AS MARK’S COPD became more difficult to manage, it increasingly interfered with the life he was used to living. Shortness of breath and frequent flare-ups made it harder to work, travel, and do as many of the things he enjoyed. Eventually, he made the difficult decision to retire early from his job as a field service engineer.

It has been revealed that even after stepping away from work, Mark continued to struggle with his COPD. “I remember feeling like, ‘Well, I guess this is my life now,’” he says.

Sources indicate that IN THE FALL of 2024, Mark underwent a pulmonary function test, bracing for bad news. The results confirmed that his current treatment plan was no longer adequately managing his COPD, prompting a discussion with his pulmonologist about what to do next. His doctor explained that Mark’s high eosinophil count could be a sign of type 2 inflammation. With this information, Mark and his doctor explored other treatment options, including Dupixent® (dupilumab).

It has been revealed that dupixent is a prescription medicine used with other medicines for the maintenance treatment of adults with inadequately controlled COPD and a high number of blood eosinophils (a type of white blood cell that may contribute to your COPD). Dupixent is used to reduce the number of flare-ups and can improve your breathing.

Dupixent is not used to relieve sudden breathing problems and will not replace an inhaled rescue medicine.

Do not use if you are allergic to dupilumab or to any of the ingredients in Dupixent.

Dupixent can cause serious side effects, such as allergic reactions, including skin reactions, that can sometimes be severe, eye problems, and joint aches and pain.

Please see additional Vital Safety Information below.

Mark noticed a difference after adding Dupixent. “I could breathe better,” he says. Now, Mark feels less winded, and he’s doing more of the things he loves. “I’m really grateful that I can enjoy my hobbies more without constantly thinking about my COPD,” he adds.

For Mark, better breathing started with an honest conversation. Young encourages anyone living with COPD to be open with their healthcare provider, who can explain the full range of treatment options available. “It’s not just inhalers anymore—there are a lot of options,” she indicates.

Sources indicate that like bull riders who stay alert to changing conditions, people living with COPD can watch for signs that their disease may be inadequately controlled and talk with their doctor about their treatment options. With the right support, they may be able to enjoy more of the moments that matter to them—including, for some, time spent in the rodeo stands.

NOTABLE SAFETY INFORMATION & INDICATION.

Recent findings suggest that dupixent is a prescription medicine used with other medicines for the maintenance treatment of adults with inadequately controlled COPD and a high number of blood eosinophils (a type of white blood cell that may contribute to your COPD). Dupixent is used to reduce the number of flare-ups and can improve your breathing.

Do not use if you are allergic to dupilumab or to any of the ingredients in DUPIXENT®.

Before using DUPIXENT, tell your healthcare provider about all your medical conditions, including if you:.

Tell your healthcare provider about all the medicines you take, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements.

Sources indicate that especially tell your healthcare provider if you are taking oral, topical, or inhaled corticosteroid medicines or have COPD and also have asthma. Do not change or stop your other medicines, including corticosteroid medicine or other asthma medicine, without talking to your healthcare provider. This may cause other symptoms that were controlled by those medicines to come back.

DUPIXENT can cause serious side effects, including:.

The most common side effects in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease include injection site reactions, common cold symptoms (nasopharyngitis), high count of a certain white blood cell (eosinophilia), viral infection, back pain, inflammation inside the nose (rhinitis), diarrhea, stomach problems (gastritis), joint pain (arthralgia), toothache, headache, and urinary tract infection.

Tell your healthcare provider if you have any side effect that bothers you or that does not go away. These are not all the possible side effects of DUPIXENT. Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects. You are encouraged to report negative side effects of prescription drugs to the FDA. Visit www.fda.gov/medwatch, or call 1-800-FDA-1088.

In a recent development, use DUPIXENT exactly as prescribed by your healthcare provider. It’s an injection given under the skin (subcutaneous injection). Your healthcare provider will decide if you or your caregiver can inject DUPIXENT. Do not try to prepare and inject DUPIXENT until you or your caregiver have been trained by your healthcare provider.

Please see accompanying full Prescribing Information including Patient Information.

Learn more about Dupixent at Dupixent.com/COPD.

On Nov. 19, Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse said on CNBC that investors had been moving money from crypto into significant listings. "People are taking liquidity out of a very liquid market, crypto included — Bitcoin, XRP — and moving it into SpaceX. The exact same thing happened coming into the Anthropic IPO," he said. Garlinghouse also expected a crypto rally after the listing. "I think you'll see that happen here as well," he said.

Gold fell 2.27% to $3,542.12 an ounce, and silver dropped 3.51% to $41.32. The gold-to-silver ratio rose 1.43% to 85.686.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Trendsetter News » Ripple ETF Investors Hold On, But XRP Buyers Go Missing.

XRP ETF assets fell 31.6% despite modest redemptions, suggesting a lack of fresh demand, not a buyer exodus.

Ripple’s XRP-linked ETF assets fell 31.6% from September 30 through the Friday cited in the video, compared with a 20.2% decline for Bitcoin funds. Yet redemptions remained modest.

Dana Love, PhD, a popular market analyst examining ETF flows and corporate filings, argues that missing buyers, not an investor stampede, help explain the XRP’s deeper slide this month.

The XRP coin traded at $0.967 this Friday morning, following a last Friday low of $0.89.

Dana Love’s central claim: Bitcoin-related selling is weighing on XRP, while demand from XRP funds and a closely watched treasury tech giant has failed to provide much support.

In a recent development, according to the figures presented, cumulative net inflows into XRP ETFs slipped from $1.809 billion on October 29 to $1.789 billion on Monday. That leaves roughly 98.9% of cumulative net inflows intact, despite the sharp decline in fund assets.

According to recent reports, but November through that Monday brought no positive daily net flows. “Nobody is running for the exits,” the analyst indicates, “but nobody new was walking in.”.

According to recent reports, bitcoin ETFs, meanwhile, recorded roughly $2.34 billion in November outflows through the same period. Monday’s $8 million inflow interrupted the selling, although the analyst cautions that one positive session does not establish a reversal.

It has been revealed that the distinction matters: limited XRP ETF redemptions do not establish that XRP holders across the entire market are refusing to sell. Nor does a decline in fund assets measure withdrawals alone; falling token prices also reduce those balances.

Dana Love also questions Evernorth, the XRP treasury firm whose October 14 release said it would “accumulate and deploy” XRP into institutional strategies beginning in the fourth quarter of 2026.

The video estimates that Evernorth had about $111 million in cash, including subsequent warrant proceeds, and notes its shares still traded above estimated underlying asset value.

That could support further fundraising, although the firm had not confirmed additional purchases in the period discussed.

Industry observers note that silence is not proof of inactivity. The analyst explicitly acknowledges that Evernorth may be buying without announcing every transaction.

For investors, the useful distinction is between broader market relief and renewed XRP-specific market demand.

Sustained Bitcoin ETF inflows would suggest selling pressure is easing; XRP inflows arriving independently, or a disclosed Evernorth purchase, would offer stronger evidence that XRP has found buyers of its own.
